title: One signature, many actions
takeaway: Reject any request that bundles several actions or upgrades your wallet unless you asked for exactly that.

cards.title: One click, three actions
cards.body: A site promises a free egg in one click. You tap Claim. Your wallet shows a single request, but inside it are three actions. Only the first is the egg you wanted.

value.label: The claim you wanted
value.why: This is the part you asked for.

value.label: Hidden unlimited approval
value.why: You never asked to approve your tokens.

value.label: Hidden NFT transfer
value.why: This moves your dragons to a stranger.

cards.title: What one confirm can hide
cards.body: Since an Ethereum upgrade in May 2025, a standard called EIP 7702 lets a normal wallet act like a smart account. One confirm can run several actions together. Honest apps use this to save steps. Scam sites use it to pack approvals and transfers into one request.
points: Read every action. Reject if even one is unwanted.

cards.title: Upgrades happen inside your wallet app
cards.body: The upgrade uses your wallet app's own contract. You turn it on or off there. Real apps can open your wallet's own upgrade prompt. The danger is a delegate that is not your wallet's own contract. When unsure, reject; single actions still work.
points: Undo an upgrade in your wallet app settings.
revoke.cash can show it, but cannot undo it.

cards.title: Real cases, real scope
cards.body: ScamSniffer's 2025 report lists two cases of $1M or more that used batch signatures, $2.54M in total. That counts large cases only. A leaked key makes batches more dangerous, because a thief with your key can upgrade your wallet themselves and take anything you later send to it. Guard your seed phrase.

cards.title: Try it
cards.body: A site asks to upgrade your account. Tap each red flag, then Done.

value.label: Requesting site
value.why: Real apps can open your wallet's own upgrade prompt.

value.label: Network name
value.why: The network name is not the problem.

questions.stem: A batch request lists Claim egg and Approve all NFTs. You only wanted the egg. What do you do?
options: Reject the whole request
Confirm, the egg is listed first
Confirm, then revoke later
Confirm if the fee is low
questions.why: The risk is what the batch contains. One action you did not ask for means reject everything.

questions.stem: A DM says: upgrade your wallet to a smart account now or lose your presale spot. What do you do?
options: Ignore it, upgrade deadlines in DMs are lures
Upgrade fast using the link in the DM
Ask the sender which contract to delegate to
Upgrade only your mint wallet, to be careful
questions.why: Your wallet app offers its own upgrade. A DM or site pushing an upgrade with a deadline is a lure.

questions.stem: You turned on a smart account and now want to undo it. Where do you do that?
options: In your wallet app's account settings
On revoke.cash with one click
On any site that offers it
By asking support in a DM
questions.why: You undo a delegation inside your wallet app. revoke.cash can show it but cannot remove it.

questions.why: Only the egg was yours. The hidden approval and NFT transfer would let a stranger take your USDC and dragons. Reject the whole batch.

questions.stem: You turned on your wallet's own smart account in its settings. Where is the risk now?
options: In what each later batch request contains
In the upgrade itself, so undo it
Nowhere, smart accounts block scams
In your public address being seen
questions.why: Your wallet's own upgrade is not the danger. The danger is a scam site packing harmful actions into a batch you confirm.

questions.stem: What does EIP 7702 let a normal wallet do?
options: Run several actions in one confirm
Reverse a transfer after it is sent
Block every scam site automatically
Hide your address from websites
questions.why: EIP 7702 lets a normal wallet use smart account features, like batching several actions into one confirm.

questions.stem: revoke.cash shows a delegation on your account that you do not recognise. What do you do?
options: Undo it in your wallet, from a clean device
Click revoke on revoke.cash, which removes it fully
Leave it, delegations can only batch your actions
Ask a helper in the chat to remove it
questions.why: revoke.cash can show delegations but cannot undo them. Undo it in your wallet. An unknown sweeper delegation can also mean your key leaked.

seg.label: Pushed upgrade
seg.why: A deadline from a stranger is pressure, not a real need.

seg.why: A DM link, not your own wallet app's prompt.

seg.label: Confirm a batch
seg.why: You cannot see what this batch contains.

questions.why: No real team DMs you to upgrade. Upgrades happen inside your wallet app, and an unknown batch can hold anything.

questions.stem: A batch shows two actions, then says and 3 more you cannot open. What do you do?
options: Reject unless you can read every action
Confirm, the first two look fine
Confirm if the site looks official
Confirm it, but from a smaller wallet
questions.why: The risk is what the batch contains. If you cannot read every action, reject it.
